chapters.title: Deborah is waiting!
chapters.quote: You brought a rescue party. Good. Now bring a plan.
text: Somewhere inside a towering prison of shipping containers, Deborah is waiting for you. The passages change. The guards grow stronger. The Warden has a toilet. You have thirty minutes.

Gather one to four Heroes, cross the colored gates, hunt down the Black Keycard, and defeat Gordon. Levels 1–19 rescue nineteen different damsels; Level 1 begins with Nessa. Deborah herself waits at Level 20, where Hector the Director stands between Gordon’s defeat and her rescue. From Level 21 onward, Gordon steals cash instead. SECURE THE BAG, then see how far the server can go!

This booklet uses the game's default keyboard and mouse controls. Its little-console-booklet look is a tribute; your adventure runs in Garry's Mod. Rebound game actions follow your configured bindings.

chapters.title: Your first rescue
steps: In staging, visit the Hermit. Choose Fighter, Rogue, or Wizard and settle your first feat choice. Collect your starter weapon.
Press P to inspect your character. Use Equipment to choose gear, and I to set your spell. Read any unfamiliar effect before entering.
Use the portal. The first Hero entering each dungeon starts its 30:00 collapse clock.
Find the cards and open their gates: Red, Blue, Yellow, then Black. Neil carries the Black Keycard.

Defeat Gordon; at Level 20, also defeat Hector’s Director’s Heart in the court. Collect the Jail Key at the arena center, open the rescue chamber, then touch or use the current damsel to complete the level. From Level 21, recover the marked cash case instead.
chapters.quote: Beating the Warden isn't the rescue. Come and get me!

chapters.title: Take the controls
rows: Cast selected Magic; drink if holding a Healing Potion
Select an owned weapon or equipped throwable
Use the object in front of you
Toggle Equipment open/closed (rebindable in Equipment; console command lod_equipment)
GPS / Haste toggle, when their feats are owned
text: Wallet and Manual share the Player Menu's tabs. Special Moves use arrow-key sequences; their alternate keys can be rebound in Equipment. Menus do not pause this multiplayer world or its clock.

In the Spellbook, click a Form with LMB or RMB to bind RMB, or click it with M3, M4, or M5 to bind that mouse button. Binding labels appear on the Forms. Your selected Content applies to all bound Forms; bindings stay with your character through reconnects and dungeon transitions. A single-Form character keeps RMB casting.

chapters.title: Keep this book with you
text: Press P, then choose MANUAL. You can read here in staging, inside the labyrinth, or while spectating. You do not need to return to the book stand.
Facing the staging book and pressing E opens this very same Manual tab. It remembers your page and reading position when you leave or switch tabs.

Use Previous and Next, choose a chapter from the contents list, or search for a word such as 'poison' or 'Black Keycard'. Arrow keys turn chapters when you are not typing. The mouse wheel scrolls long pages. Text-size controls enlarge the print. Escape closes the menu.
The terminal TIME OVER sequence takes over the screen and input until its restart prompt. Reading does not stop danger, grant protection, or stop time.
chapters.quote: One book. Two ways in. No excuse for getting lost.

chapters.title: Back in staging
text: Staging comes before Dungeon 1 and after each successful rescue. Speak to the Hermit, inspect your character in the mirror, check the Heroes of Legend board, and visit the Debbie statue for your wallet collection.

Your first Hermit visit issues one identity-bound advanced starter weapon; reopening the conversation does not issue another. Later staging visits offer one standard random-drop gift. Finish pending class and feat decisions, then choose your loadout.

Completing a dungeon resets the collapse clock to 30:00. It stays paused through the celebration and your return to staging, until the first Hero enters the next dungeon. Your weapons, magazines, reserve ammunition, equipped gear, stored items, and consumable stacks stay with your Hero.
The portal commits you to the active dungeon. A Hero who remains behind cannot pause the countdown for teammates already inside.

Each rescued damsel stays in the staging room for the rest of the campaign. Approach her and press E for a short conversation and service. Restoratives refresh once per dungeon visit; equipment, the rescue fund grant, and the reserve life are once per Hero identity per campaign. Reconnecting does not renew a claim. Gifts you cannot use remain unclaimed.

The roster is Nessa, Bessa, Tessa, Odessa; Nell, Belle, Estelle, Mirabelle; May, Faye, Kay, Desiree; Jean, Colleen, Maureen, Josephine; Dora, Cora, Eleonora; and finally Deborah. Early families share complementary clothing and accents. The final four keep their natural appearances.

The first five replenish Pistol, SMG, Shotgun, .357 and AR2 ammunition respectively. Belle heals, Estelle cures ailments, and Mirabelle restores Magic. May through Maureen gift gloves, a ring, boots, headwear, a vest, trousers and a shield. Josephine supplies a Healing Potion; Dora restores full health; Cora grants 25–75 Debs; Eleonora restores one reserve life up to the normal maximum. Generated gear gifts cannot be resold or fused.

After Deborah’s Level-20 rescue, she takes the Hermit’s place in staging. There is only one Deborah: approach her at the old guide position and press E for Abundance. The pedestal still provides the same one-time starter or one stored gift per dungeon visit; speaking to Deborah does not issue another. She remains your host throughout the endless campaign. A fresh campaign restores the original staging cast.

After Deborah’s rescue, Gordon announces his new vocation: stealing cash for the love of the game. Dungeons continue indefinitely with increasing encounter pressure and bounded enemy counts. The rescue roster resets with the campaign; persistent wallet records and Abundance cooldowns follow the existing server wallet rules.

chapters.title: Thirty minutes. One campaign.
text: Each dungeon has 1,800 seconds. Its clock starts when the first Hero commits to entering the labyrinth. A successful rescue resets the next dungeon clock to 30:00; it stays paused through staging until the first Hero enters.
Death, Tetris, menus, map use, staging visits, spectating, and disconnections do not pause or extend this clock. An empty server does not bank extra time for your return.

At zero, a seven-second prison demolition ends in GAME OVER: THE PRISON HAS COLLAPSED. A fresh campaign starts automatically 20 seconds after the collapse finishes. After five seconds of aftermath, PRESS E TO START A NEW GAME restarts sooner at Dungeon 1 with a fresh clock and roster.
A rescue completed earlier in the campaign does not exempt the party from the eventual timeout.
chapters.quote: I appreciate the sightseeing. I would appreciate the rescue more.

chapters.title: Follow the keycards
rows: Find Red Keycard → open Red Gate
Find Blue Keycard → open Blue Gate
Find Yellow Keycard → open Yellow Gate
Find Neil → defeat Neil → take Black Keycard
Open Black Gate → enter Gordon's arena
Defeat Gordon → at Level 20, defeat Hector → take Jail Key → open chamber → rescue damsel / secure cash
text: The labyrinth spans connected floors, stairs, passages, and gates. Its required route is solvable; a gate is a progression barrier, not a wall to bypass with a movement trick.
Watch the current objective and your floor. A target above or below you may require the stairs, not a turn into the nearest corridor. Defeating Brute alone never awards the Black Keycard.

chapters.title: Read the maze
text: Press M for your map. It consumes Magic while open and suppresses Magic regeneration. At the base rate, a full 100 Magic lasts 15 seconds; Wisdom and applicable equipment or feats alter the cost. At zero Magic the map closes.
Use short looks to check your floor, route, and current objective. The map is information, not a pause screen. Your build determines available breadcrumbs and other navigation aids.

GPS requires its feat. Press G to toggle its private voice without spending Magic. When enabled, stand still for one second with no living enemies within two cells on your floor. It gives a direction, then can repeat after four seconds of silence. Movement, combat, or nearby enemies cancel the cue—even if those enemies are behind walls.
GPS follows the current legal objective route. It does not reveal loot, monsters, or future objectives. A server with visual maps disabled can still allow GPS.

chapters.title: Who are you this time?
text: Your Hero has a generated name, appearance, Origin, Background, and Motive. Those three traits each grant a permanent perk: a favored weapon, a favored enemy, or ability points. Each chooses independently; matching perks can stack.
An ability perk gives either +2 to one ability or +1 to each of two different abilities. Read the actual trait on your Character Sheet to see what your Hero received.

Your starting scores use six rolls of four six-sided dice, dropping each lowest die. The initial array must total at least 74. A stored weakness pass then reduces the weakest score by 2d2 and the next two by 1d3 each. There is no second reroll after these reductions.
Death, reconnection, and dungeon transitions preserve your identity, class, growth, XP, and feats. A true campaign restart creates a fresh roster.
The Character Sheet groups meaningful final build statistics into Offense, Defense, Magic, Elemental, Status, Movement, Recovery and Summons / Utility. Inactive zero-value modifiers stay hidden.

chapters.title: Six scores, many surprises
rows: Physical damage; Push; Fighter shield bonus
Movement (−10% to +55% from DEX); applicable attack handling; Clumsy and fire saves
HP growth, damage resistance, regeneration; poison and bleeding saves
Magic regeneration and Arcane Shield integrity
Magic damage, approved range and utility scaling; Magic saves
text: Scores stay within 3–30. An ability modifier is floor((score − 10) / 2): 10–11 gives +0, 12–13 gives +1, and 20–21 gives +5.

Equipment changes your active combat scores, but temporary gear does not qualify you for feats. Feat requirements use your permanent character abilities. The sheet distinguishes your build from what your equipped items contribute.

chapters.title: Fighter: stay in the fight
text: A Fighter regenerates toward 33% of maximum HP from Level 1. After five continuous seconds without effective damage, regeneration starts at 1% of maximum HP per second, modified by Constitution. Damage restarts the delay. This does not refill temporary Tetris overfill.

Second Wind, Rapid Recovery, and Unbroken add 11%, 22%, or 33% to the ceiling; higher ranks replace lower ranks. A Fighter with these reaches 44%, 55%, or 66%. Other independent gear contributions can also help.
A Fighter protects half of a positive Strength damage modifier, rounded up, from Constitution reduction. The remaining part is reduced normally. This is a flat damage bonus, not a percentage bonus.

With a shield equipped, a Fighter also adds positive STR modifier percentage points to Block: STR +5 adds five points. All Block sources share one roll and a 33% cap. No shield means no class Block bonus.

chapters.title: Rogue: keep moving
text: Rogues gain 11% ordinary voluntary movement speed in every direction, or 22% total while sprinting. The class itself adds no jump-height bonus.

Rogue Dodge contributes 11 percentage points ordinarily and 22 at the fast movement tier. Dodge needs actual voluntary speed: below one quarter of walking speed it is zero. Below 90% of sprint speed, the combined cap is 33%; at or above it, the cap is 66%. Forced movement and jumping do not manufacture extra Dodge. Magic cannot be Dodged.
Rogue damage dice have better explosion thresholds: d6 continues on 5+, d12 on 7+, and other eligible dice on their maximum. Sealed rolls such as generation or healing are not damage explosions.

A direct attack from behind Backstabs: it ignores all Constitution damage reduction and adds one damage multiple. Normal ×1 becomes ×2; aimed ×2 becomes ×3; Deadeye ×3 becomes ×4. Passive and status damage do not Backstab.

chapters.title: Wizard: spend wisely
text: A Wizard receives one extra distinct Content at Level 1 and is the only class that can acquire and cast SUMMON. All classes can use their other owned Forms and Contents.

Arcane Shield automatically diverts part of incoming resolved HP damage into Magic. It begins at 10%, adds 2.5 percentage points per Level, and stops at 50%. Intended diverted HP rounds upward. Normally one Magic pays for one diverted HP; unpaid damage still reaches HP.

Magical damage can test Arcane Integrity and shatter the shield. Physical hits can trigger Feedback under its class rules. Arcane Shattered disables the shield until recovery. These are automatic defenses, not voluntary spell casts.

Magic capacity is always 100. INT 10 regenerates at the base rate; INT 20 at about 1.71 times that rate; INT 30 at three times the rate. Low INT never falls below 85% of base regeneration, but an open map suppresses that regeneration first. Living Aegis improves shield efficiency, not pool size. Non-Wizards can instead obtain the Mana Barrier feat family; Wizards cannot draft it.

chapters.title: A Wizard’s bright ideas
text: Arcane Surge rewards a full Magic pool. An eligible attack committed at full Magic receives a bonus equal to your positive Intelligence modifier. Its commitment snapshot matters: spending the spell’s cost does not retroactively erase an earned full-pool bonus.

Feedback is a reactive counterattack. When an eligible hit deals HP damage to a Wizard whose shield is online, Feedback’s chance equals your current diversion fraction. A successful response has a one-second cooldown. It rolls one d4 for each actual die in the incoming damage contract, including continuations, then adds positive INT modifier.

Feedback is Magic damage, but does not add Wisdom or recursively trigger Feedback. An Arcane Shattered shield cannot produce this response. The separate Feedback Loop feat restores Magic from eligible damage-die continuations; read its entry for the per-cast cap.

chapters.title: Read the resistance
text: Monsters and controlled Soldiers have lighter defenses than Heroes: Constitution removes at most 1 HP per damage die, and Arcane Shield absorbs at most 30% without rounding small hits away. Hero Constitution, shield and Feedback rules stay as described in their class entries.

Enemy Feedback has at most a 15% chance and a two-second cooldown. Magical hits have an easier shield-break check; a successful break disables diversion and Feedback for at least 24 seconds, or 1.5 times the rolled duration if longer. A break or defeat also cancels a still-pending retaliation.

Read the combat feed for the reason and a useful response. Backstabs bypass Constitution; larger hits lose less to its per-die reduction. Magic can break Arcane Shield, while Poison bypasses diversion. True Faith resists Magic, so try physical attacks. Mind Over Matter resists a physical hit, then leaves a recovery window for your follow-up.

chapters.title: Grow into a legend
text: Heroes begin at Combat Level 1 with 100 base HP. Later Levels use a stored class hit die: Fighter d10, Rogue d8, Wizard d4. Constitution's per-Level HP bonus is capped at +6. Reopening the sheet or reconnecting does not reroll growth.
The current Hero Level ceiling is the lower of 20 and Dungeon Level +3. XP earned at the temporary ceiling is banked until the ceiling rises. Level 20 uses 96,000 total XP, after which Hero XP stops.

A kill awards 40% of its XP to the finisher and shares 60% by HP damage contribution. Defeating a human Soldier does not yield Hero XP. Each deployed Hero receives rescue XP of 500 + 100 × min(Dungeon Level, 20).

Choose one of three stored feat offers at Levels 1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18. Pending choices do not reroll on reopening, death, or reconnection. Level 20 adds one class capstone choice. There are no extra Rogue feat drafts at Levels 2, 5, 10, or 15.

chapters.title: Choose your specialty
text: A feat may require permanent ability scores, a previous rank, a weapon or Magic capability, or a particular actor type. The draft filters these requirements before presenting three distinct offers. Choose one; the other two are not yours.

Ranked families usually replace their own lower rank. Separate sources add only where their rules say they do. Six repeatable fallback feats can raise individual permanent abilities when offered, up to the intrinsic score ceiling.

The reference chapters at the back include every current ordinary feat, all six fallbacks, and the nine class capstones. Their requirements and effect descriptions come from the same catalog used by the game.

Wall Jump grants four successful kicks before landing, each requiring a fresh Jump press near a static vertical wall. Holding Jump and touching a wall do not refill them. Cloud Step is separate: spend 3 Magic once before landing for a double-impulse extra jump. Hold a direction for a modest horizontal boost. Wall Jump takes priority when a legal kick is available. These jumps retain their full strength; invisible walls above the crates block maze shortcuts while leaving legal upper-floor paths and stairs open.

chapters.title: Every hit tells a story
text: A damage expression such as 2d6 means two six-sided dice. Eligible damage dice can explode: a qualifying result adds another die, which may continue the chain. Generation, progression, healing, and other sealed rolls do not inherit damage explosions.

Strength adds once to a physical damage contract per target; Wisdom does the same for Wisdom-scaled Magic. Constitution reduces positive die contributions, with the ordinary minimum-one rule. Strength and Wisdom are flat additions, not percentage multipliers.

Aimed and Backstab multiples, equipment, elements, Dodge, Block, and Arcane Shield then matter according to their rules. A zero or immune attack does not become damaging merely because a bonus exists.

Watch the lower-right readout, or press L for the Die Log. Both display the same authoritative events: rolls, saves, damage, Dodge, status effects, regeneration, Magic, Push, XP, and more. A DODGE can be recorded even when damage is zero. Names and labels carry meaning as well as color.

Nearby player rolls appear in your Die Logger. Wisdom expands your listening range. Look directly at a teammate to see their username as their character, in the same semantic colors. Active ailments replace the HUD character name, color the portrait and trigger an onset cue; afflicted enemies show matching effects and status events.

chapters.title: Know your weapons
rows: Base 1d3; no ammunition. Bash and Walloper improve it.
1d6 with a minimum contribution of 3 per damage die; shared shell damage and strong hit stun.
1d10 projectiles; one cartridge powers a three-shot burst.
1d12 with special exploding chains and penetrating shots.
text: Dice are the starting point, not guaranteed final damage. Your abilities, class, feats, aimed hits, range, armor, and elemental matchup can change the outcome.

Right mouse casts your chosen spell while a normal weapon is held. It does not use the stock game's grenade launcher or alternate-fire attack. Ordinary explosive grenades are not part of this equipment economy.

chapters.title: Fire with a little finesse
text: SMG heat rises as you fire. Its baseline heat threshold is six; heat cools in quarter-second steps, and overheating locks it for two seconds. Watch and listen for warm, near-overheat, and ready feedback. Heat-control feats change the weapon's limits.

The Pulse Rifle has a 0.45-second tell before a three-projectile burst, with 0.09-second spacing and 0.25-second recovery. The whole baseline burst spends one cartridge. Burst-size feats add projectiles through this same attack.

The Revolver uses a special d12 continuation ladder: the fresh die explodes at 8+, then later thresholds descend through 7, 6, and 5 in its ordinary chain. Rogue and relevant feats change eligible thresholds. Its magazine progress builds bonuses, and its later shots can fire extra projectiles. It also has a baseline 25% chance to conserve a cartridge.

The Shotgun rolls 8 plus an independent exploding d6 for pellet count, capped at 36. Shell damage is divided into six shares and applied according to each target’s pellet hits, with the normal minimum-one rule. Its hit stun is four times the ordinary duration. The pellet-count roll is utility, not damage, so damage feats do not inflate it.

chapters.title: Hold steady. Then fire.
text: The Revolver can enter an aimed state after you keep position and aim still for a base 0.5 seconds. An aimed shot deals ×2. Moving, changing your aim, switching weapons, or attacking breaks or consumes the state. Faster-aim effects reduce the required hold.

Deadeye makes the Revolver’s aimed multiple ×3 and lets the other supported ordinary weapons aim for ×2. A Rogue’s qualifying Backstab then adds one more multiple. Holding right mouse is not the aiming command; right mouse is your Magic control.

The Revolver’s cylinder adds a flat bonus equal to chambers already spent: ordinarily +0 through +5. Its fifth cartridge fires two projectiles; its sixth fires three. Below 60 HP, each HP below 60 adds one percentage point of chance for one extra projectile. Below 34% maximum HP, each full percentage point below 34 adds one point of chance to preserve the final cartridge. These conditional chances are separate from its baseline 25% ammunition conservation.

chapters.title: Make every round count
text: Total carried includes the loaded magazine. All copies of one weapon family share ammunition; collecting another copy does not create an independent ammo reserve.

Passive recovery prevents complete deadlock. Below the normal one-magazine floor, ammunition returns gradually after an interruption delay. The times above are the base empty-to-floor recovery schedules; firing and applicable feats affect recovery. It is not a full-ammo refill.
Ammo pickups favor an owned family with room. Reload deliberately, use the crowbar when appropriate, and save powerful shots for threats that deserve them.

chapters.title: Put a spell together
text: Open I for the Spellbook. Choose an owned Form to decide how the spell travels, then an owned Content to decide its element and rider. Cast with the Form’s bound mouse button (RMB by default). The Form's base cost and the Content's surcharge combine before applicable cost rules.

Every Hero begins with one random direct-damage Form and RAW Content. Wall and Summon never replace that starting spell; Wizards may learn them through later grants. Wizards receive an additional distinct Content at Level 1. The normal Content grants occur at Levels 4, 8, and 14. Only a Wizard can acquire or cast SUMMON or WALL.

Magic tops out at 100. Intelligence governs regeneration; Wisdom governs spell power and approved range, radius, and utility scaling. A spell's visible area boundary marks its actual area, while a Beam ends where world geometry stops it.
When holding any throwable, its controls take priority. Switch back to a normal weapon to cast.
Spellbook labels distinguish READY / AVAILABLE, LOCKED, NEED MAGIC, COOLDOWN, and BLOCKED. Solid floors stop all spell areas. Open stairwells and shafts still allow exposed vertical hits.

chapters.title: Ten Forms of Magic
rows: 3d6; immediate forward force cone, 64° wide. WIS scales reach; Content supplies its element and rider.
2d6; connected visible cells around the caster. Solid walls and floors block damage.
3d6; piercing line, 0.65-second cast recovery. Stops at solid geometry.
3d6; lobbed area attack. Throw range fixed; radius scales with WIS.
3d6; steerable projectile with area impact. WIS affects range and radius.
4d6; fast precision shot. No area or body piercing.
2d6 per contact; a chaotic bouncing ball can strike several enemies or return to the same one. Six-second lifetime, up to six hits, at most two active per caster. Walls and floors redirect it.

Roll 1d6 bounces on throw. Enemy contacts deal 1d6 with a brief per-target cooldown; the last bounce shatters for 2d6 area damage. Lower base blast radius than Bomb, with WIS radius scaling. Expires after eight seconds; clear rind/flesh effects mark the shatter.
Wizard only: call a gold Seeker for 20 seconds. Default cap: one.

Wizard only. A barrier up to 288 units wide, 112 high and 12 thick fits nearby clear space; WIS increases its 10-second duration by two seconds per positive modifier, up to 30 seconds. Heroes pass through; enemies are blocked and take 2d6 contact damage. The server preview shows the actual fitted shape and placement reason. Only one active Wall per caster. Hold its bound mouse button to see the aiming guide; release to place. Opening a menu cancels the pending placement.
text: Numbers beside names are base Magic costs before Content. A summoned Seeker carries the selected Content into its attacks. An invalid placement that cannot find safe ground and hull clearance fails without spending Magic.
Beam can hit each eligible body along its resolved line once. Its blue/cyan core remains recognizable even with an elemental accent.

chapters.title: Give your spell a character
text: A rider is an attempt, not a guaranteed condition. The attack must deal qualifying damage to a surviving target; then the appropriate save or Morale rules apply. A duplicate guaranteed rider does not secretly create repeated rolls for the same event.
Contents are class-neutral. A Fighter or Rogue may attach any Content they own to a Form they can use. Summoning itself remains Wizard-only.

chapters.title: Find their weak side
text: Each generated monster independently has a one-in-three chance of elemental affinity. If it has one, the six elements are equally likely. An Earth creature resists Earth and is weak to Electric; the same reciprocal rule applies to each pair.

The other four elements and untyped damage remain neutral unless another explicit effect says otherwise. Weakness and resistance use their own single-roll ladders, from 11% through 88%; do not assume several visible sources mean several separate reduction rolls.

An elemental aura and aimed elemental words help identify affinity. Class tint and elemental affinity are different clues: a Rogue or Wizard can have any element. Gear may add elemental damage, wards, or a weakness. Read both the benefit and the drawback.

chapters.title: Trouble you can shake off
rows: Slower movement and impaired attack handling; 1+1d4 seconds.
Burning damage; recovery checks can extinguish it.
Loses HP on cell movement; periodic saves can clear it.
Repeated damage ticks with recovery saves.
Disrupts restraint; AI can turn on nearby allies.
Arcane Shield is offline until recovery.
Brief player disruption from failed Morale.
text: The listed ability is the relevant condition-save lane. Many durations are rolled, so repeated applications need not last equally long. Status riders and feat procs still respect their saves. Reapplication follows the condition's own refresh rule, rather than creating unlimited copies.

chapters.title: Dodge, Block, Push, Morale
text: Dodge combines eligible sources into one speed-gated roll against physical attacks. Block combines eligible sources into another shared physical defense, capped at 33%. Neither is a promise of invulnerability. Wizard diversion spends Magic after ordinary mitigation.

Push is a resolved attack effect, not free movement. Strength, size, equipment, and relevant feats affect its attempt and distance. A legitimate wall collision can become a wall slam; ordinary contact with scenery is not automatically bonus damage.
Hit stun can interrupt a hostile's preparation. Watch telegraphs: canceling a charge is different from trying to stop an attack that has already been released.

Morale compares the attacker's Charisma pressure with the defender's save when a qualifying trauma or effect calls for it. A failed check can make an AI flee; a player receives the authored brief Intimidated response instead of losing the controls to AI. Cooldowns prevent every pellet from demanding another Morale check.

chapters.title: Dress for the rescue
text: Equipment has a bag and dedicated slots. You can keep multiple copies of a weapon family and select the one to equip. Touching a pickup stores the item; it does not silently replace your carefully chosen gear. Procedural pistols and crowbars drop from Dungeon 1 alongside the other early weapons, even if you already own the starter versions.

Wearable families are headwear, vest, trousers, boots, rings, gloves, and shields. A ring can use either hand. A pair of gloves occupies both hands; displacing it frees both. The shield uses the left-arm accessory slot, not a ring slot.

Your ordinary equipment storage holds 32 records, including equipped gear. The inventory shows only the actual free equipment slots and an exact used/total counter. Consumables appear below the gear grid with their separate per-type stack limits. Only equipped wearables and the currently wielded weapon contribute their effects. A powerful weapon sitting in the bag does nothing to your current attack.

Drag equipment onto a highlighted valid slot to equip; drag it into the bag to stow. Drop unwanted, unequipped equipment onto the visible trash can to destroy it immediately with a disposal sound. Protected progression objects cannot be trashed. The server confirms the final position after every action.

Weapon identity uses a soft aura, distinct muzzle behavior, and two independently selected tints while preserving a canonical grip or stock. Each stock weapon has three physical regions while wielded, in a teammate’s hands and as a pickup, including models with a single native material. Tint A follows the element; Tint B follows a mechanical trait family, with shades derived from the individual roll. Surface patterns are retired. Wintery means Ice, including Wintery Warding and Wintery Frailty.

chapters.title: Read the fine print
text: Current generated gear also has one drawback and one elemental damage identity. Weapons always carry a hit rider. An item's effect depends on its actual rolls; a grand name alone is no guarantee it suits your build.

Equipment power scales with Dungeon Level up to 999, even after Hero Level stops at 20. Quality and family affect its budget; paired gloves account for their two occupied slots. Value is a comparison score, not cash in hand.

Properties can affect abilities, saves, damage, speed, Dodge, Block, regeneration, Push, map cost, breadcrumbs, summons, elemental wards, weaknesses, and hit riders. Conditional damage bonuses say when they work: injured, almost stationary, or highly charged with Magic. The equipment-property reference lists every current property.

chapters.title: Supplies in the corridors
text: Ordinary drops are character-owned. A pickup you can inspect is not necessarily an item another player can claim. Walk into your eligible pickup to collect it. A full bag or full consumable stack leaves an unaccepted pickup available rather than silently destroying it.

Early dungeons offer more need-aware assistance: resource shortages and long dry spells can influence useful drops. This help decreases through Dungeons 2–10; from Dungeon 11 onward the assistance layer no longer provides pity, objective guarantees, deficit steering, or resource-budget supplements. Base random loot remains.

Normal ammo pickups add up to 6 Pistol rounds, 3 Shotgun shells, 9 SMG rounds, 6 Pulse Rifle rounds, or 2 Revolver rounds, limited by room. The carried caps still include the magazine. Equipment drops, consumables, and temporary ammunition are ordinary run inventory; they are not persistent DFTs.

chapters.title: A bottle for a friend
text: Healing Potions, Stink Bombs, Summon Cards and Feathers of Resurrection each stack up to three. Equip a stack in the Throwable slot, then select it as your held weapon. Its controls appear on screen.

Healing Potion: right mouse drinks it to restore up to 25 HP. At full ordinary HP, drinking is rejected without consuming one. Left mouse throws it; the first living allied Hero hit receives the healing. There is no healing splash. A missed throw still spends the bottle.
Stink Bomb: left mouse throws a five-second poison cloud with a 96-unit radius. Enemies entering make the normal Constitution save against Poisoned. You cannot drink a Stink Bomb.

Summon Card: choose another deployed Hero. Left mouse brings them to a safe adjacent square; right mouse brings them to your square or its nearest safe equivalent. Closed gates still apply. A cancelled or failed selection spends nothing.

Feather of Resurrection: either mouse button restores the oldest eligible zero-life Hero in the Hero Queue with exactly one life, preserving their character and surviving inventory. Active Soldiers and Soldier respawn waits are excluded; returning to the Hero Queue restores eligibility. Full Hero slots defer admission. No eligible Hero means no Feather spent.
These bottles, cards and Feathers spend no Magic. Holding one replaces spell controls; switch weapons before trying to cast a spell.

Healing Potions are remedies: they also clear every active negative condition, even at full HP. Magic bombs cover Physical, RAW, all six elements and every condition. They share normal throwable slots and saves; their 144-unit explosion cannot hit through solid walls or floors.
chapters.quote: The red one is medicine. Please read the label.

chapters.title: Equipment with a trick
rows: Psychic Crush · Crown of Psychic Crushing
text: Quickstep dashes forward up to 90 units over 0.2 seconds; walls stop it. Ordinary voluntary-speed Dodge rules apply. It is not permission to cross a locked gate.
Rebuff sends a one-cell burst of 1d6 untyped Magic, followed by a 96-unit Push attempt against surviving damaged enemies.

Psychic Crush targets the nearest visible enemy within two connected maze cells. Closed gates and solid cover block it. It deals 2d8 plus your Wisdom bonus as Magic; the enemy makes a Wisdom save for half damage. The die readout identifies the target and save. With no valid target, you spend no Magic. The Crown is at least Rare and its innate power is included in its value.

You must equip an item that grants the move. Enter its sequence with the arrow keys. The default alternate keys map Up to [, Down to comma, Left to semicolon, and Right to backslash. Rebind those mirror keys in Equipment if needed.
Pause more than 0.8 seconds between inputs and the sequence resets. An unavailable move, insufficient Magic, or an active cooldown cannot be bypassed by entering the combination faster.

chapters.title: Gloves of the Fighting Streets
text: These paired gloves occupy both hands and grant both techniques while equipped. They are at least Rare; their affixes and innate techniques contribute to their value. Stowing them removes the techniques.

Ember Fist launches a straight elemental fireball up to five cells (1920 units), dealing 2d6 plus Wisdom as Magic to the first enemy hit. Solid cover stops it; there is no splash or piercing. The gloves’ affinity determines the element and its ordinary Content rider: Earth Push, Fire Immolated, Dark Poisoned, Ice Held, Light Muted or Electric Morale.

Cinder Rise strikes visible enemies in your current maze square for 2d8 plus Wisdom as Magic, using the gloves’ element. Surviving damaged enemies attempt the ordinary Immolated save. Its upward effect does not move your Hero; walls and floors block its hits.

Both use ordinary offensive Magic cost modifiers, without a Content surcharge. A committed miss still costs Magic. An invalid source, blocked launch, insufficient Magic or cooldown spends nothing. Stale fireballs disappear if you die, change roles or dungeons, or remove the source gloves; they do not refund Magic.
Rebuff uses the same sequence as Ember Fist, but its ring cannot stay equipped alongside these two-hand gloves. Read your equipped item’s details before entering the sequence.

chapters.title: Ring of Invisibility
text: This single-hand ring grants up to 12 seconds of Invisibility while equipped. It is at least Rare and can occupy either hand. Paired gloves displace it. Its generated properties and innate technique both contribute to its value.

AI enemies lose you as a target while invisible. Their shots already in flight, committed area attacks, environmental hazards, and manually aimed human Soldiers can still hurt you. Sixth Sense can reveal your silhouette under its ordinary visibility rules.

Primary or secondary attack input reveals you, even if the attempt is dry or blocked. Magic on any bound button, an offensive item technique, a throw attempt, or dealing or taking HP damage also reveals you. Walking, jumping, reloading, opening menus and drinking a potion alone preserve Veil.

Removing or moving the source ring, death, a role or dungeon change, and other lifecycle transitions end Veil. It cannot refresh while active. Ending never refunds Magic or resets the cooldown. Failed activation spends nothing; Veil costs a fixed 20 Magic.

chapters.title: Hat of the Thunder God
text: This Rare-or-better headwear grants Thunder Charge while equipped. Its generated properties and innate technique both contribute to its value. Stowing or replacing the Hat ends an active charge.

An electric-blue path and sound warn for a quarter-second, then you charge straight along your original aim for up to three blocks in 0.8 seconds. You cannot steer. Walls, locked gates, actors, stairs, ledges, wet or harmful spaces stop the charge. Start on a supported flat floor with at least 32 units of safe room.

The first enemy contact deals one hit of 2d8 plus Wisdom as electric Magic, with its normal Morale rider. Surviving enemies that lose HP may suffer ordinary hit-stun, subject to their existing immunities and retrigger rules. Allies stop your charge without taking damage. There is no piercing or splash.

The charge grants no invulnerability, flight or extra Dodge. It uses ordinary offensive Magic cost modifiers and reveals Veil. Failed activation is free; once committed, interruption or a miss does not refund Magic or reset the cooldown. Removal, death, role or dungeon changes, forced movement, Held or Muted cancel it.

chapters.title: Boots of the Heavy Plumber
rows: Land from above · Passive · No Magic cost
text: These Rare-or-better boots occupy your feet slot. Equip them before leaving solid ground, then land on an enemy from above to deal 2d6 plus Strength as physical damage. Your usual dice, defenses and damage modifiers apply. Sideways contact and landing on allies do not attack.

A valid stomp gives you a short upward rebound, even if the enemy dodges or blocks the damage. Low ceilings reduce the rebound. With insufficient clearance or unsafe floor support below, you land normally without an attack. The Boots do not grant flight, invulnerability or protection from fall damage.

You get one stomp attempt per airborne excursion, with at least 0.65 seconds between commitments. Your bounce is part of that same excursion. Land on solid, non-actor support to rearm; standing on an enemy or swapping Boots in midair will not do it.

Heavy Stomp needs no arrow sequence or Magic. Muted and holding a potion do not disable it; Held does. A committed stomp reveals Veil. Removing the Boots or changing life, role or dungeon invalidates the armed landing.

chapters.title: A little more time
rows: LMB / RMB: USE · Adds 2d4 minutes · Stack of 3
text: This rare consumable buys the whole party more time. Equip and hold it in the Throwable slot, then press either mouse button. One Hourglass is consumed; the server rolls two ordinary four-sided dice and adds their sum in minutes to the current dungeon clock. The Die Log shows both dice, and everyone's clock updates immediately.

The result is always two through eight minutes: no exploding dice, class bonuses or Magic cost. Any Hero class can use it, with the ordinary 0.6-second item cooldown. A stack holds at most three, and each legitimate use adds its full result even above 30:00.

Use it before time runs out. At or after the deadline, TIME OVER wins; the Hourglass cannot reverse the collapse. Paused staging clocks, failed or cleared dungeons, Soldier bodies and unequipped items cannot spend it. Successful rescue resets the next dungeon to 30:00, while unused Hourglasses remain in your Hero's inventory.

chapters.title: Boots of the Moon
rows: 25% lower gravity · Passive · No Magic cost
text: Equip these Rare-or-better boots in your feet slot for higher jumps and longer airtime in the dungeon. Gravity is reduced by 25%; ordinary steering and horizontal movement remain yours to control. No arrow sequence, Magic cost or cooldown is required.

Your usual jump, Cloud Step and Wall Jump impulses still apply. Float On keeps its own controls and Magic cost. Invisible maze walls, locked gates, collisions and fall damage remain in force: these boots do not grant flight or invulnerability.

Removing or replacing the boots restores ordinary gravity, including in midair. Their effect ends on death, staging or role change and returns when the same equipped boots belong to a living, deployed Hero again. Human Soldiers cannot borrow the Hero's equipment.

chapters.title: Tanuki’s Ring
rows: Stand still for 2 seconds · Passive · No Magic cost
text: Equip this Rare-or-better ring in either hand and stand still on solid ground for two continuous seconds. You become stone: enemies stop seeing and targeting you, and direct hits, explosions, hazards and damaging statuses cannot take your HP while Statue remains active.

Movement immediately ends Statue, including jumps, crouching, forced propulsion, moving supports and teleportation. Attacking, casting Magic, using an item or interacting also ends it, even if the action fails. Dealing HP damage ends it too. You must stand still for another full two seconds; looking around alone is allowed.

Statue costs no Magic and has no fixed duration or cooldown. It does not cure existing conditions or stop the dungeon collapse clock. Removing or moving the ring, dying, changing role or changing dungeon cancels it. An interrupted connection cannot retain an old activation.

Other players can see your stone body. A brief original transformation chime and stone flourish mark activation, and STATUE appears above your status portrait. Separate sources of invisibility retain their own rules.

chapters.title: A little borrowed sorcery
rows: LMB: piercing Beam · 12 charges · No reload
text: Each Wand is a distinct procedural weapon with its own twelve-charge pool. Equip a copy through Equipment and press LMB to attempt a Beam. One accepted attempt spends one charge and no personal Magic, with at least0.65 seconds between attempts. RMB still casts your selected Spellbook Magic.

Wizards activate Wands normally. Rogues make one non-exploding d100 roll:5% success at Level1,50% at Level10,95% at Levels19 and20. A failed Rogue attempt still consumes the charge and cooldown but produces no Beam. Other classes cannot activate it. Muted and Intimidated prevent activation without spending a charge.

A successful Wand Beam deals3d6 plus Wisdom through the shared Magic combat rules. It pierces eligible bodies once each in order and stops at blocking architecture or its normal range, extended by your existing spatial bonuses. Its cyan core keeps the familiar Beam identity; the Wand affinity supplies elemental damage and color accents.

The Wand uses its rolled equipment status chances and normal saves after effective damage; it does not add a second automatic Content rider. Your normal compatible damage modifiers and defenses still apply. Wand use does not unlock Beam or a Content in the Spellbook, and spending a charge does not count as spending personal Magic.

The remaining charges are always shown while the Wand is held and in its Equipment description. Empty Wands remain in your inventory. Reloading, ammunition pickups, regeneration, swapping copies, weapon recreation, respawning and dungeon transitions never refill a copy. Stored and frozen copies preserve their recorded charges. Attack attempts reveal Veil and end Statue.

chapters.title: Down, but not finished
text: Heroes start with three lives. On death, your weapons, magazines, reserve ammunition, equipped wearables, stored gear, and throwable potions stay with your Hero for the respawn. Your character identity, XP, class, feats, and persistent DFT collection remain too. Reconnecting does not restore a lost life or reroll your character.

A normal death has a mandatory 20-second respawn lockout. Play Tetris while waiting, or spectate. After the lockout, press F to finalize your reward and respawn. You can keep playing until the normal 60-second death-Tetris maximum, when respawn happens automatically.

At zero lives, press F3 for three choices: wait for resurrection, begin a new Level-1 Hero, or join the Soldiers. Beginning again discards that character's carried gear and progression but preserves account $DEB and DFTs. All Heroes may be eliminated without resetting the dungeon; only the collapse timer ends a failed run. Someone must still reach the rescue objective to clear it.

Successful rescue can bring eliminated teammates back under the campaign's comeback rules, up to the maximum of four lives. A revived Hero returns with the same saved weapons, ammunition, wearables, stored gear, and throwable potions.

chapters.title: Make room for a comeback
text: Move pieces left or right, rotate with Up/Forward, soft-drop with Down/Back, and hard-drop with Jump. Clearing several lines at once earns the corresponding reward, not the sum of separate single-line clears.

Rewards become temporary HP overfill. They do not permanently increase maximum HP and cannot be refilled by ordinary regeneration. Topping out ends the board session while preserving the bonus already earned; it does not erase the mandatory death wait.

After rescue, Victory Tetris lasts 20 seconds. Russian Asset doubles qualifying HP rewards in both Tetris modes. It also raises the death-Tetris maximum to 120 seconds, but F still becomes available after the same 20-second lockout. It never extends Victory Tetris or the active dungeon clock.

chapters.title: Friends—and human foes
text: Up to four players take cooperative Hero roles. Up to six additional players can control enemy Soldiers, for ten active players; further arrivals spectate. Role availability and the Soldier queue determine when an incarnation can be entered.

A human Soldier receives a generated monster character, class, abilities, and automatically selected feats. The player does not draft Hero feats. A fresh incarnation is a fresh Soldier character, not the revival of the previous build.

Human Soldiers can earn incarnation-local XP and automatic Combat Levels, capped by Dungeon Level +3. AI Soldiers do not earn XP. Monster-side Levels can reach 999. Soldier play preserves your eliminated Hero; return to the Hero Queue to become eligible for resurrection.

The Debbie Fund can reward Soldier-attributable Hero life losses after a successful rescue. Switching into Soldier play forfeits that player's Hero share for that dungeon. The fund does not award a rescue pool for a timeout.

chapters.title: Meet the prison staff
text: An enemy's archetype tells you how it fights; its class, Combat Level, feats, and element make that particular creature different. Normal tier chances are 60% Typical, 30% Elite, and 10% Champion, using Dungeon Level, +1, and +2 respectively. A tier is a Level change, not a secret second set of damage multipliers.
Shamblers threaten close quarters; Runners close gaps quickly. Deadcrabs are low jumping attackers. Soldiers use ranged fire; Blitzers press aggressively; Snipers punish exposed sight lines.
BioBlasters threaten with biological attacks. Watchers demand attention to their readable attack tells. Seekers telegraph a committed charge: move out of its path instead of retreating along it.

Listen, look ahead, and use corners. Killing an enemy does not guarantee a permanently safe floor; wandering populations can replenish. Size, class tint, elemental aura, and aimed information help you decide what to tackle first.

chapters.title: More unwelcome company
rows: Pink fast-zombie silhouette; climbs to reach you. Watch vertical approaches.
Stationary gas hazard. Do not stand beside it.
Red soldier silhouette; warns before a short-range fire attack.
Oversized headcrab with a telegraphed fire attack.
Stationary gun emplacement; break its firing line.
Flying blade with a warned dive. Move off its committed approach.
Marks a target area before its Magic strike. Leave the mark.
Ceiling ambusher with a venom shot. Look up.
Stationary sweeping laser. Interrupt its charge or use cover; gunfire will not cancel an already released beam.
text: Fire can attempt Immolated; venom can attempt Poisoned. These enemies use the same saves, damage, elements, and progression rules as the rest of the roster.

chapters.title: The control detail
rows: Icy-blue Vortigaunt. Its Ice attack marks a fixed patch of floor before erupting. Leave the mark or interrupt the charge: a failed Wisdom save can leave you Held while its Runner closes in.
Pale-ivory Combine elite. A visible line warns of a straight, non-homing Light bolt. Sidestep or take cover. A failed Wisdom save can leave you Muted; guns and melee remain available.
Brown-and-gold Vortigaunt. It warns before an Earth pulse around its fixed casting position. Leave the ring or take cover. The hit can push you into a Soldier’s firing line.
text: These specialists appear with ordinary attackers. Identify the control threat early, then choose whether to interrupt it, evade its commitment, or remove its companion.

Held and Muted use the ordinary saves and recovery rules. Their warning colors identify the attack; a creature’s class and elemental affinity still belong to that individual. Cover and movement remain useful answers for every class.

chapters.title: The prison support detail
rows: A slave Vortigaunt channels recovery into one wounded ally. The green link announces a 1.5-second window to interrupt it or break its line of sight. Each completed channel restores 12% of the ally’s maximum HP, rounded up and capped at 24 HP; it cannot revive the dead.

A Combine elite protects one ally with a blue tether. Its six-second guard adds 25 percentage points to ordinary physical Block, still capped at 33%. Magic bypasses Block. Kill or interrupt the Bulwark, draw the ally more than 240 units away, or break the tether with cover.

A Metrocop calls up to three nearby allies onto one visible Hero for four seconds. The gold call changes their target priority without adding damage or speed. Break sightlines, interrupt the caller, or turn the pursuing group into your team’s firing line.
text: These enemies support existing companions; they neither summon reinforcements nor revive fallen enemies. Support does not stack. When nobody qualifies for support, each specialist can still fire a weak ordinary projectile.
Their distinctive links and call warnings remain visible with reduced effects. Generated class and elemental affinity are independent of the support role.

chapters.title: Watch the other route
rows: A purple Combine soldier takes a legal alternate approach around the lane where it saw you, using a short loop or a two-leg flank within its own room. Its split chevron gives a brief warning before it moves. Watch the side approach, change lanes, or interrupt it; it cannot cross a locked gate or follow an unseen change of direction.

A cyan Metrocop commits a visible firing line and releases one straight projectile before withdrawing. Its backward chevrons announce the retreat. Dodge the shot, then close the gap or deny its cover; interrupting the wind-up prevents the planned withdrawal.

An amber Combine elite marks a reachable junction with a square and cross. You have one second before it starts walking there. Take a different exit, interrupt it, or beat it to the junction. The marker deals no damage; its ordinary gunfire still warns before release.
text: These specialists move through ordinary passages. Their plans are brief commitments to the position where they last saw a Hero, not knowledge of movement behind walls. Gates, obstructions, disabling conditions and interrupted plans can foil their maneuver.

Pincers appear beside Soldiers, Harriers beside Shamblers, and Waylayers beside Runners. Their route warnings remain visible with reduced effects. Generated class, health and elemental affinity still belong to the individual.

chapters.title: Make their response your opening
rows: The steel-blue Combine elite braces behind a shield-shaped tell. After a short warning, its guard stays aimed in one direction for 2.5 seconds. Frontal physical attacks face an extra Block chance, capped at 33%; it cannot walk or shoot while braced. Use Magic, circle to a flank, interrupt it, or wait for the guard to end. The ground arc shows the protected direction.

The rose-colored Metrocop answers a direct damaging hit with a hooked-arrow warning and one straight projectile. Its one-second wind-up gives you time to sidestep, take cover or interrupt it with another damaging hit. It does not reflect your damage, and damage over time does not trigger the response.

The rust-red Combine soldier normally fires from range. A direct hit that leaves it at 40% health or less can provoke one wounded rush: a jagged chevron announces the approach, followed by a one-second warning along its fixed lunge direction. Step aside or obstruct it. The lunge has three seconds of stationary recovery, shown by open bars; healing to 60% health rearms a later rush.
text: Pavises appear with Runners, Reprisers with Soldiers, and Redliners with Shamblers. Watch both members of the pair: their different attack rhythms create different openings.
These responses keep ordinary class defenses, statuses and damage rules. Held stops the guard and lunge; Muted does not stop physical shots. Their warnings remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Read the whole shot path
rows: The cyan Combine soldier draws a shot path with a diamond at its possible wall bank. After a 1.1-second warning, the physical projectile can ricochet once along the reflected line. Dodge the first lane and watch the second. New cover absorbs it; without a suitable wall it fires straight.

The amber Metrocop warns along a fixed lane, then sends a shot beyond the position where it saw you. The shot pauses for three quarters of a second, marked by a hollow diamond, before returning to its original launch point. Sidestep, then stay clear until the return passes; cover stops either leg.

The mint-green Combine elite draws two parallel lanes for 1.2 seconds. Its paired shots leave the center open: hold that gap or move completely outside the lanes. There is no hidden middle shot. Cover and an interrupted wind-up can stop the volley.
text: Caromers appear with Shamblers, Reelers with Runners, and Forkers with Soldiers. Companions can pressure the safe space, so read both attack rhythms. These are physical shots governed by ordinary class defenses and conditions.

Hit-stun can cancel the warning. A shot already in flight keeps its frozen path; it never follows a moving Hero. Each pattern can damage a given Hero at most once, including both Forker lanes. Reduced effects retain the path warnings.

chapters.title: Leave yourself an escape
rows: The cyan-and-orange Combine soldier marks a short tripwire across a lane. A hollow diamond and thin boundaries give 1.25 seconds of warning before it becomes live for five seconds. Endpoint posts and the upper rail show its jumpable height: jump above the wire, walk around either end, wait it out, or interrupt its maker. The narrow floor outline shows the full danger strip.

The blue Vortigaunt arms a fixed circular snare after one second. It stays armed for at most six seconds. Entering with enough time left triggers one snap 1.25 seconds later, announced by inward teeth and a shrinking bar. Leave the circle to bait the snap safely; it cannot follow you or reset its timer. The Ice hit can leave you Held under the ordinary save rules. Mute, interrupt or defeat the Snarer to cancel it.

The orange floor turret is a destructible pressure node. Two concentric rings warn for 1.5 seconds before one physical pulse, followed by a brief recovery. Enter the safe center, leave the outer ring, take cover, or interrupt or destroy the node to open the approach. The center stays safe; this is a single pulse, not lingering gas.
text: Wirewrights appear with Runners, Snarers with Soldiers, and Cordons with Shamblers. Their companions pressure different escape routes; watch the whole encounter before committing.
These traps stay where they were marked. Thin boundaries and a hollow diamond mean arming; thicker boundaries mean live. Their finite warnings and escape routes remain visible with reduced effects.

A trap can hit a given Hero only once. Damage, defenses and conditions follow the ordinary combat rules. Interrupting or destroying the maker cancels its trap; removal never leaves a hidden hazard behind.

chapters.title: Respect the second swing
rows: The green-tinted zombie marks a broad semicircle in front of itself for 1.1 seconds, then sweeps it once. Back beyond the arc, circle behind it, take cover or interrupt. Its facing stays fixed through the warning; exploit the 2.5-second stationary recovery.

The ochre fast zombie marks two nested, narrow attack sectors. After one second it strikes the inner sector; 0.85 seconds later it strikes the longer outer sector along the same fixed direction. Sidestep and wait for both beats. Rushing straight back after the first swing can put you into the second. It then recovers for 2.8 seconds.

The pale-violet Metrocop shows a dashed retreat path and steps backward, then warns for 0.9 seconds before a long, narrow thrust from its marked endpoint. Resist chasing straight after it; move sideways out of the rectangle. Obstructing the retreat or interrupting the warning stops the attack. It recovers for 2.5 seconds.
text: Reapers appear with Soldiers, Drubbers with Runners, and Fencers with Shamblers. Their companions can contest the space you need to escape, so read the entire encounter.

All three make physical melee attacks under ordinary damage and defense rules. Interrupting them ends the commitment. Held stops a Fencer’s backstep but permits stationary strikes; Muted does not stop physical attacks. The fixed shapes and beat countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Watch what you leave behind
rows: The rust-orange zombie fights at close range. Defeating it leaves a fixed orange circle and shrinking bar around its corpse: after 0.8 seconds it bursts once. Back outside the circle or use cover before collecting its ordinary drop. Killing it stops its living attacks, but does not erase this warning.

The green fast zombie can claim a nearby defeated ally when injured. A crossed-jaw mark, tether and shrinking bar announce 0.6 seconds of stationary feeding. Interrupt, kill or separate it, break the tether with cover, or defeat it before its Shambler escorts. A successful meal restores at most 30 HP, capped at maximum health. It gets one attempt per corpse and waits six seconds before another.
text: An Afterburst appears with a Soldier; Carrion travels with Shamblers. Carrion can consume an Afterburst before it bursts, extinguishing the circle. Neither action creates another enemy or an extra reward; consumed remains still yield their ordinary drop on schedule.

Both enemies also warn a narrow, fixed melee sector. Sidestep or interrupt it. Held permits their stationary attacks and feeding; Muted does not stop these physical actions. Circles, tethers and countdowns remain readable with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Break the line, cross the screen
rows: The teal Metrocop marks a fixed narrow corridor and inward-pointing chevrons for 1.2 seconds. Sidestep, close inside 96 units, leave the lane or interrupt it. A successful physical hit can pull you a short distance toward it, subject to the ordinary push save. Blocked damage prevents the pull. Walls and missing floor support prevent movement. It then rests for three seconds.

The blue Combine engineer warns a slatted screen for one second, then holds it for three seconds. This screen is freely passable. It adds 25 percentage points to ordinary physical Block for up to three allies behind it when your attack crosses the screen; the combined chance still caps at 33%. Flank, walk through, use Magic, interrupt the engineer or wait. The engineer itself receives no protection from its screen. Without suitable allies it fires an ordinary physical shot.
text: Towline appears with a Runner; Screenwright appears with a Soldier. Read the whole encounter: the companions can exploit a pull or shelter behind the projected screen. No extra bodies or rewards are created.
Both channels remain stationary and interruptible. Held and Muted do not prohibit these physical actions. Their frozen shapes and countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Leave the route, mind the trail
rows: The amber Combine soldier outlines its entire short route for 1.2 seconds, then carries a dangerous 64-unit circle along it. Step sideways out of the outlined lane, take cover, interrupt it or defeat it. Once movement begins, the thick ring follows its actual position. The carrier stops at its destination or after 1.8 seconds; it cannot steer after you.

The green Metrocop warns a short retreat route for 1.2 seconds. Dashed circles show where it may leave up to three 44-unit patches as it reaches those points. Each placed patch becomes a thin solid ring for another 0.8 seconds before turning thick and dangerous for 1.2 seconds. Leave the circles or wait; chasing directly along the trail is risky. Unreached points never become damaging patches.
text: Each whole commitment can hit a given Hero at most once, for physical damage under ordinary defenses. These enemies choose routes with escape space; they cannot carry hazards through locked gates or unsupported floor. Their paths stay fixed and their hazards expire.

Interrupting, defeating or holding the source cancels the movement and every associated patch. Muted does not stop these physical actions. Cover blocks damage. Dashed plans, solid warnings, thick danger boundaries and shrinking countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Footsteps and sightlines
rows: The amber Metrocop hears non-crouching footsteps in its own room. Its paired-ring marker and dashed route show a brief investigation toward that sound. Crouch, stop making footsteps, or change course after the cue. It does not track your hidden movement.

The violet fast zombie remembers a visible Hero, then advances toward that last-seen position only when no eligible Hero has line of sight to it. Its crossed-eye marker announces the fixed route. Keep a clear sightline, use a teammate to watch the lane, or relocate behind cover. Camera direction does not matter.
text: Investigations warn for 0.8 seconds, travel at most 128 units, and end within another 1.4 seconds. Movement itself deals no damage. Listener needs fresh hearing and clear sight to strike; Shy can strike a visible Hero who comes close. Each melee attack has a separate 0.9-second, fixed narrow arc: leave it, use cover, or interrupt.

Their memory is brief and confined to a supported room. Invisibility prevents acquisition; they cannot follow you through walls, closed gates or missing floor. Interrupting or holding them cancels investigation; Muted does not silence physical footsteps or attacks. The dashed route, distinct destination glyph and countdown remain visible with reduced effects.

Listener is deliberately footstep-sensitive: gunfire and generic sound effects do not feed its hearing. A crouching Hero can still be threatened by its ordinary companions. Shy remains visible; its rule never forces you to aim or look in a particular direction.

chapters.title: Cure the ailment, break the bargain
rows: The pale-cyan slave Vortigaunt draws a crossed-diamond tether to an ailing ally and channels for 1.5 seconds. It removes one existing negative condition, without restoring HP. Interrupt or mute the Absolver, separate it from its ally, or break their sightline. A cure that has already happened cannot be taken back.

The crimson Combine elite marks an ailing Hero’s position with a 64-unit circle and crossed diamond for 1.25 seconds. Leave the circle, cure the selected Bleeding, Immolated or Poisoned condition, break sight, or interrupt it. The mark never follows you. A successful physical hit consumes that ailment; ordinary Block and Dodge still apply. With no qualifying ailment, Exactor fires an ordinary warned shot.
text: Absolver accompanies Shamblers; Exactor appears with a Flamer. Avoiding the Flamer’s Immolated attempt deprives Exactor of that opportunity. Exactor threatens only the Hero it marked, and each warning permits at most one hit.

Cleansing targets one condition in a fixed order, not every ailment. If that condition ends during either warning, the commitment fails; a new application needs a fresh warning. Neither enemy applies a new condition or creates extra bodies.

Held allows these stationary actions. Muted interrupts Absolver’s cleansing Magic but does not prevent either enemy’s physical shots. The tether, glyphs and shrinking countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Together — or apart?
rows: The sand-colored antlion singles out an isolated Hero. Its lone bracket glyph and narrow, frozen melee arc warn for 1.1 seconds. Bring an eligible teammate within 192 units on the same floor with clear sight to cancel the attack; alone, leave its arc, retreat or interrupt. The strike reaches 112 units and deals physical 1d6+2 before ordinary defenses.

The pale-blue Vortigaunt marks exactly two nearby Heroes with linked 64-unit circles for 1.4 seconds. Separate beyond 160 units, leave either frozen circle, break its sight to either Hero or break the pair’s sightline to cancel the whole link. Each marked Hero risks one Raw Magic 1d6+2 hit. With no eligible pair, it fires an ordinary warned Raw projectile that a solo Hero can evade.
text: Both attacks commit to the original Heroes and positions; replacement Heroes and later arrivals do not inherit a warning. No attack tracks hidden movement or adds a lasting field. Outrider recovers for 2.4 seconds after its attack.

Held permits these stationary attacks. Muted cancels Conductor’s Magic; Outrider’s physical strike remains available. Interrupting or defeating the source cancels its pending warning. The isolation glyph, arc, paired circles, linking line and countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Protect your Magic — interrupt theirs
rows: The violet Stalker marks a Hero’s position with a fixed 64-unit circle, downward funnel and 1.25-second countdown. Leave the circle, break its sight or interrupt or mute the caster. A hit deals Raw Magic 1d6+2 through ordinary defenses. Only a surviving Hero who actually loses HP also loses up to 12 current Magic; the Siphoner gains none. A fully absorbed, blocked or dodged hit has no additional drain. It recovers for 3.5 seconds.

The gold slave Vortigaunt marks a Hero with a fixed 64-unit circle and lightning glyph for 1.25 seconds. Its Raw Magic 1d6+2 attack spends 40 Magic before its ordinary cost modifiers. When it cannot afford that attack, a battery-and-plus glyph over its own position announces a two-second self-recharge instead. A completed recharge restores up to 45 Magic, capped at 100; interrupt or mute it, force it to move or break its sight to cancel the refill. It recovers for 2.5 seconds.
text: Both resource attack marks threaten only the original Hero and never follow movement. Leave the circle or break sight before release; later arrivals and replacement lives do not inherit the mark. An Accumulator with an ordinary cast-triggered Aura Burst feat can also deal supplemental aura damage to other nearby Heroes, including those who escaped its circle. That separate feat never adds a Magic-drain rider. Arcane Shield and other defenses keep their ordinary behavior. These enemies do not steal loot, currency or permanent stats.

The Accumulator’s recharge creates no damaging circle and needs no ally: its battery glyph and countdown expose an opportunity to pressure it. Canceling a recharge still leaves its recovery period. Held permits stationary attacks and recharging; Muted cancels both enemies’ Magic. The drain, lightning and battery shapes and shrinking countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Turn their fire against them
rows: The copper Combine soldier freezes a narrow firing lane for 1.25 seconds. Its arrow and body-bracket glyph warn where the single physical shot will go. Sidestep or place an ordinary enemy in the lane: the first body intercepts the shot, including one of its companions. Walls absorb it. The Fusilier then recovers for three seconds.

The ochre Combine elite marks a fixed 72-unit circle with a fragment glyph and 1.6-second countdown. Leave the circle and lure ordinary enemies into it: the physical blast can hit them too. A body cannot shield you from this area attack, but solid cover can. The circle stays where it was placed when you move away. The Bombardier then recovers for 3.5 seconds.
text: Both attacks deal physical 1d6+2 before ordinary defenses and threaten only actors present when the warning began. Later arrivals and replacement lives do not inherit damage; an unmarked body can still absorb the Fusilier shot harmlessly. Neither enemy harms itself. Named bosses, their clones, event actors, friendly summons and human-controlled Soldiers are excluded from this friendly fire.

Interrupt, defeat or displace the attacker, or break its sight to cancel the warning. Held and Muted do not stop these stationary physical attacks; morale flight and hit-stun do. The firing lane, blast circle, distinct glyphs and countdowns remain visible with reduced effects. These two enemies do not make the rest of the prison fight among themselves.

chapters.title: Stop — or keep moving
rows: The amber Combine elite tethers one Hero with an octagonal pause glyph and the literal command STOP. During the final 0.4 seconds, keep voluntary speed below one quarter of your legitimate walking speed.
The cyan Metrocop tethers one Hero with double chevrons and KEEP MOVING. During the final 0.4 seconds, maintain voluntary speed at or above one quarter of your legitimate walking speed.
text: Each demand warns for 1.6 seconds. PREPARE becomes JUDGMENT for the final 0.4 seconds; the countdown, thicker glyph and quarter-bar bracket identify that interval. A violating observation during judgment commits one physical 1d6+2 hit at release, subject to ordinary defenses. Comply throughout the interval to avoid it. Earlier movement does not decide the result.

The tether follows only the originally captured Hero life. Only one demand can hold a Hero at a time, including across both enemy types. Break sight with solid cover, leave the 360-unit range or current cell, or interrupt or defeat the source to cancel the demand. Later arrivals and replacement lives never inherit it.

Only actual voluntary motion counts: movement input against a wall is not enough for KEEP MOVING. Forced pushes, Held, nonwalking movement or stale motion evidence cancel the demand harmlessly, rather than making a forced failure count. An interval without enough reliable movement evidence also cancels.

Held and Muted on the attacker permit these stationary physical demands; morale flight and hit-stun cancel them. STOP and KEEP MOVING text, distinct glyphs, tether and countdown remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Break the bodyguard and the oath
rows: The blue Combine elite warns BODYGUARD for 0.8 seconds, then moves its own body along the frozen route toward an ally’s firing line. Its shield glyph stays on its actual body. Flank, change angle, use piercing or area attacks, interrupt, or defeat it. The route never follows your new position; its arrival hold lasts at most two seconds.

The violet Metrocop warns OATH for 0.8 seconds, then binds one ordinary ally for three seconds. If that exact ally is legitimately defeated during the armed oath, the broken-oath glyph and RETALIATION announce a separate, full 1.2-second shot warning against the original Hero. Prioritize the Mourner, break the tether, wait out the oath, or defeat its ally and evade the warned shot.
text: The Interposer grants no Block, immunity or damage diversion: ordinary body interception alone can protect the ward, so protection is never guaranteed. Held prevents its movement. The Mourner grants no resurrection or extra rewards; an old corpse cannot trigger its oath. The killer does not become a new retaliation target.

Without an eligible ally, either enemy warns SHOT for 1.2 seconds. Every fallback or retaliation shot freezes the original Hero’s visible position when that shot warning begins, then releases one physical 1d6+2 packet before ordinary defenses. Leave the fixed lane, use cover or another body, or interrupt the attacker. The first actual body or wall blocks the shot; an intervening enemy is not damaged by it. Each attack ends in three seconds of recovery.

Only one bodyguard or oath can reserve an ordinary ally at a time. Breaking sight, leaving range, displacing the stationary source or ward, or defeating the source cancels the commitment. Held permits stationary oaths and shots; Muted permits these physical actions. Morale flight and hit-stun cancel them. BODYGUARD, OATH, RETALIATION and SHOT labels, route or lane, distinct shield or oath glyphs and countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Cease fire or find refuge
rows: The ochre Combine soldier marks one Hero with a crossed-barrel glyph and CEASE FIRE. PREPARE lasts 0.8 seconds; WATCH lasts 2.4 seconds. Starting a firearm, crowbar, Magic or Wand attack during WATCH triggers a separate, full 1.2-second RETALIATION warning. Stop attacking through WATCH, interrupt or defeat the Censor, break sight with solid cover, or leave range.

The mint Vortigaunt freezes a 144-unit threat ring around your initial position for 1.6 seconds. REFUGE marks a safe pocket of radius 48, displaced 96 units from the ring center. Enter that pocket or LEAVE RING before judgment. Both routes are checked for your actual body when the warning starts. The rings and arrows stay fixed when you move.
text: The Censor observes new committed attacks, not damage: passive effects, ailments, earlier projectiles and equipment actions that do not commit an attack cannot trigger it. Retaliation freezes your visible position when its new warning begins. Leave the fixed lane, use a wall or intervening body, or interrupt the source. The first body or solid cover absorbs the shot; an intervening enemy is not damaged. The single physical hit is 1d6+2 before ordinary defenses.

The Surveyor releases one physical 1d6+2 hit only if the originally marked Hero remains inside the outer ring and outside the refuge at judgment. Solid cover, leaving range, interrupting or defeating the Surveyor also cancels it. Muted cancels Surveyor judgment; Held does not. Other enemies can still threaten either escape route: refuge protects only against this judgment.

Each commitment belongs to the original Hero life. A death, replacement life, reset or invalid geometry cancels it; nobody else inherits the warning. Held and Muted permit the Censor’s stationary physical actions. Morale flight and hit-stun interrupt both enemies. Three seconds of recovery follow each commitment. Labels, distinct glyphs, fixed geometry and countdowns remain visible with reduced effects.

chapters.title: Neil has the Black Keycard
text: After Yellow Gate, look for Neil: the green-suited bureaucrat clutching a briefcase. Neil flees through the open labyrinth and across connected floors. He does not attack you. He alone carries the Black Keycard.

Brute is his independently killable antlion-guard escort. It keeps near Neil and reacts when you hit him. Orange warning marks a charge: after a 1.25-second preparation, Brute commits to its direction. Sidestep that line. A wall collision stuns it for two seconds.
You may defeat the escort first, but Brute is not an invulnerability switch. Neil can be defeated independently. Take the Black Keycard dropped by Neil to progress.
Neil is fixed at Dungeon Level. Brute is fixed at Dungeon Level +1.

chapters.title: Gordon the Warden
text: Beyond Black Gate is a two-level arena: a lower court and an upper gallery. Gordon is the heavy man in a pig mask. Entering commits the encounter and closes the back gate.

An entry or respawn alcove provides protection and one aid allowance per Hero identity per dungeon: up to 25 HP, up to 30 ammunition per owned gun, and one Healing Potion. Repeated entry is not an unlimited supply.

Above roughly 60% HP, Gordon alternates a three-second cloak with a visible warning before launching four slow homing orbs. Around 60%, he rides his toilet and leaves bombs with three-second fuses. Around 25%, he clears that ordnance and charges with his crowbar.

If his cloaked phase goes twelve seconds without damage, Gordon reveals himself and pauses attacks for a two-second taunt. Hitting him ends the taunt. Crowbar stagger works once every three seconds against Gordon; gun hit stun keeps its usual rules.

Fake Gordon Clones join at Dungeon Levels 4, 8, 12 and 16, up to four. Each has one-third of the real Gordon’s maximum HP. They spread around the arena and have no boss health bar. Defeating a clone does not release the Jail Key. Defeating the real Gordon ends his fight; at Level 20 it reveals Hector instead of releasing the key.

The fight does not reset just because a Hero dies. At Levels 1–19 and 21 onward, defeat Gordon, take the Jail Key at the arena center, open the rescue chamber, and reach the damsel—or the cash after Level 20. At Level 20, defeat Hector first. Gordon’s death alone never completes the dungeon.

chapters.title: Hector the Director
rows: The Director’s Heart in the court
text: When the real Gordon falls at Level 20, an enormous, disturbingly familiar figure rises over the Flattywood horizon. Hector’s three-second reveal begins the final fight. The jail remains locked until you defeat him.

Attack the Director’s Heart: the red figure at the arena center, tethered to the giant above. This reachable core takes your ordinary weapon and spell hits. The distant body is a spectacle, not a separate target. Fight from the lower court or its upper gallery; the protected entrance permits neither outgoing nor incoming Hector damage.

Hector opens with blue missile volleys and titanic crowbar strikes. Below roughly 60% health, bombs and purple corrupted Villain of Lore bolts enter the rotation. Below roughly 25%, attacks arrive faster and ground strikes may mark several Heroes. Watch the warning text, leave fixed ground circles before impact, and dodge the traveling orbs.
