Death and revival use the normal Hero rules. Returning Heroes resume the same fight; Hector does not heal or restart because everyone temporarily leaves the court. His attacks stop while no visible, living Hero is available there. The dungeon’s collapse clock still matters.

Hector grants ordinary combat credit and enemy drops, with no separate currency prize. After his defeat, take the Jail Key, open Deborah’s chamber, and rescue her to finish Level 20. The existing Level 21-and-beyond SECURE THE BAG campaign then continues.

The familiar Hermit is revealed as Hector the Director. Only after his defeat and your successful rescue of Deborah does the finite rescue story end. Deborah succeeds him in staging; the campaign continues into SECURE THE BAG.

chapters.title: The rescue story is won
text: Deborah’s legitimate rescue begins a 6.5-second celebration inside the normal 20-second victory window. The rescued damsels cheer, and surviving participating Heroes receive her thanks and affectionate celebration beats. Your rescue rewards settle immediately; the celebration grants no extra reward.

The opening announces Deborah’s rescue, followed by the Hero celebration, then THE RESCUE STORY IS WON. Your actual Hero stays in place. Movement briefly pauses for the participating survivors, then returns. F can open the usual optional Tetris throughout the victory window and dismisses the finale view.

Reduced effects keeps your ordinary view and the story titles. If you join late, you see the current moment. Missing actors, a death or a reconnect cannot restart the celebration or pay the rescue again.

At the usual end of the victory window, return to staging for Dungeon 21. Deborah occupies the former Hermit’s position and offers Abundance through the same once-per-account, rolling 24-hour claim. Prepare your equipment, then use the portal to SECURE THE BAG.

chapters.title: The Debbie Fund
text: The Debbie Fund takes rescue funding very seriously. Its $DEB units are Debbie Coins—'Debs'—and its collectibles are Debbie Fund Tokens, or DFTs. These are server-local game records, with no cash value or outside wallet.

A successful rescue creates a pool of 100 × Dungeon Level Debs. Qualifying Soldier-attributable Hero life losses assign 11% each to the Soldier side, capped at 33% of the pool; Soldier damage contributions determine its allocation.

The remaining Hero pool is divided half equally and half by damage and effective allied healing, with hostile-loss adjustments. Eligible dead or disconnected participants can retain their claim. Switching to Soldier play forfeits a Hero share.

Rescue awards increase wallet balance and lifetime rescue earnings. DFT sales increase spendable balance but do not inflate that lifetime rescue score. The staging Heroes of Legend board records the highest dungeon reached, damsels rescued, and cash bags recovered; it is not a count of monster kills.

At Debbie, choose Fuse Equipment, Sell Equipment, Fuse DFTs, or Sell DFTs. Drag eligible items into the labeled pile, review the value, and confirm. You can also click items to add or remove them. Closing the menu cancels staging without moving anything. Sales award the displayed value in $DEB. Fusion consumes two to eight inputs and returns one legal item worth 85–100% of their combined value and more than any single input; unsupported piles are rejected intact. Equipment fusion returns carried gear; DFT fusion returns a persistent upgraded token. DFT-created gear and free starting weapons cannot be sold or fused. If any fused DFT was recreated this run, the new token remains used for this run. DFT Collection / Recreate retains the free recreation service.

chapters.title: A little something to keep
text: DFTs normally mint when a dungeon objective is completed. Combat Level milestones 1, 5, 10, and 20 can each award one token per account on this server. A rare rescue roll also gives each participating Hero a one-in-1,000 chance. Ordinary enemy kills do not mint DFTs. The treasure chest event can also award DFTs; see Treasure to keep. Rescuing Deborah at Level 20 also unlocks Abundance: visit her in staging for one free DFT per Steam account every rolling 24 hours. Reconnecting or restarting a campaign does not reset the timer. The eight-token capacity still applies; a full wallet leaves the gift available until you make room. Recreated equipment retains the usual resale and fusion exclusions.
Your collection has eight slots. Milestone items waiting for space stay frozen; making room does not reroll them. Tokens persist across ordinary death and campaign restart.
At the staging Debbie statue, recreate a token's frozen item for free once per token per run. The DFT remains in your collection. The same token becomes available to recreate again in the next run.

You may instead sell a DFT permanently for its displayed Value in Debs. Read the confirmation carefully: selling the token removes it. Wallet viewing is portable; the statue's staging, proximity, and role rules still govern its physical services.

chapters.title: Dungeon Events: discoveries and obstacles
rows: One ordinary d4: 4 pays $15 gross (+$10 net); 1–3 pays nothing (−$5 net).
25% win; 75% loss. No exploding dice or ability bonuses.
text: An enabled dungeon contains 1–4 different event types, chosen by one ordinary, non-exploding d4. A result of 1–3 selects that many from Debbie Slots, locked loot chests, vending machines, False-floor hazards, bribe blockades, Skeleton of a Hero blockades, and the Game Master’s Equipment Quiz; warp holes join this common pool from Dungeon Level 5 onward. A 4 selects three common types plus a DFT treasure event. Treasure therefore appears on 25% of event selections; its one or two physical chests count as one event type. A paired warp hole also counts once. Events never replace the required rescue objective.

Debbie Slots is optional and never blocks the rescue route. Read its posted stake and odds before pressing E to play. Each Steam account may complete one play per dungeon; reconnecting or beginning a replacement Hero does not grant another play. Other Heroes have their own attempt.

The stake uses your persistent, server-local $DEB balance, which has no cash value. A completed play applies the stake and payout together. Insufficient funds or a storage failure spends nothing and leaves your attempt available; retrying does not reroll the outcome. Leaving the dungeon ends access to that machine.
Events are enabled by default on new server configurations. Servers retaining an earlier disabled setting need an administrator to set lod_events_enabled 1 for future dungeon generation.

In developer mode, administrators can run lod_event_population_preview to generate a normal 1–4 event selection and print its locations, or lod_event_preview_generate followed by an event name for a single-event preview. Previews mark the campaign unranked but still use carried keys and persistent server-local funds and DFTs; they provide no free currency. Regenerating the same dungeon does not refresh account claims.

chapters.title: A key, or a Rogue’s touch
rows: Bag-only consumable; stacks up to nine. Press E at a locked chest to use one.
Press E without a key, or hold Sprint + E to pick while carrying keys.
5% per Combat Level, up to 95%; one ordinary d100 roll.
text: The locked loot chest sits off the required rescue route and offers each Steam account one ordinary procedural wearable per dungeon. It does not award a DFT; the item uses your normal equipment storage.

Chest Keys can appear among normal loot drops and remain in your bag rather than the Throwable slot. A key is spent only when its chest item successfully enters your equipment storage. A full bag or failed delivery spends no key; make room or retry.

A Rogue gets one lockpick attempt per chest. Failure uses that attempt but leaves any key intact, and you may later open the chest with a key. A full bag or another rejected preflight does not use the attempt. If a successful pick cannot deliver the item, retry to claim the same reward without another roll or a key.

The chest remembers your account’s claim and lockpick attempt through reconnects, replacement Heroes, and regeneration of the same dungeon. Those actions cannot grant another attempt or reroll the reward. A new dungeon provides a new opportunity; a new campaign resets the chest record.

chapters.title: Treasure to keep
rows: One ordinary d2 selects one or two optional chests; each chest offers each Steam account one DFT.
Eight DFTs. Ordinary equipment bag space does not limit this reward.
Use a Chest Key, or use the same Rogue lockpicking controls and chance as an ordinary locked chest.
text: Treasure chests hold persistent Debbie Fund Tokens, not ordinary equipment pickups. Each Hero has an independent claim at each chest. The reward is fixed: reconnecting, replacing your Hero, or regenerating the same dungeon cannot reroll it or restore a claim. Selling or recreating the awarded DFT does not reopen the chest.

Press E to spend one Chest Key when the DFT is successfully delivered. A Rogue without a key may pick the lock; hold Sprint + E to choose lockpicking while carrying keys. Each account gets one attempt per chest at 5% per Combat Level, up to 95%. A failed pick consumes the attempt but no key; you can return with a key.

A full DFT collection spends neither key nor lockpick attempt. Make room in your collection, then return. A storage failure spends no key. If a successful pick cannot deliver its DFT, the chest stays unlocked for your account: retry for the same reward without another roll or key.

Treasure events appear only on a four-event selection and contain one or two optional chests. Their DFTs persist in your server-local collection and have no cash value. Leaving the dungeon ends access to its chests. For an administrator preview, use lod_event_preview_generate treasure_chest; lod_chest_key_testkit supplies one key only if you have none.

chapters.title: A bottle for the road
rows: One bottle per Steam account per campaign dungeon. Each Hero has an independent purchase.
Restores 25 HP and cures negative statuses when used. Buying the bottle does not heal you.
Healing Potions stack up to three and use the Throwable slot.
text: Press E at a vending machine to buy one standard Healing Potion for your equipment inventory. The price uses your persistent, server-local $DEB balance, which has no cash value. The potion is ordinary run equipment, not a DFT.

Insufficient funds, a full potion stack, a storage failure, or leaving the interaction before it can complete spends nothing and leaves your purchase available. Correct the problem and retry. A successful purchase charges exactly $10 DEB and delivers one bottle.

The machine remembers your account’s completed purchase through death, replacement Heroes, reconnects, and regeneration of the same dungeon. Drinking or discarding the bottle does not restock the machine, and reconnecting does not replace a lost bottle. A new dungeon or campaign provides a new purchase.

This optional machine can appear alongside other Dungeon Events. For an administrator preview, use lod_event_preview_generate vending_machine. Purchases spend real server-local $DEB; the preview does not provide free currency.

chapters.title: Watch your step
text: A False-floor hazard is a small panel in an optional upper-floor room. Stepping fully onto it as a grounded Hero can open the floor beneath you. There is no E prompt to activate it. The solid rim around the panel gives you room to go around.

The fall leads one floor down. Ordinary gravity and falling consequences apply. The destination preserves your current progression access, and the existing stairs provide a route back; the trap never opens a locked progression shortcut.

The panel stays open for at least three seconds. It closes and rearms only after its opening is clear, so keep moving after landing. All Heroes share the same panel state, and the hazard can trigger again. If the landing is unsafe or occupied before activation, the panel stays closed.
For an administrator preview, use lod_event_preview_generate false_floor. Redeploy after generation and follow the printed locator.

chapters.title: A shorter way back
text: From Dungeon Level 5 onward, a paired warp hole may appear as an optional event. Its two cyan endpoints sit on different physical floors. The prompt identifies your endpoint and its destination floor.

Press E at either dormant endpoint. Your first successful traversal links the pair for everyone until this dungeon ends. Linked holes are free and repeatable; wait one second between your own traversals. Other Heroes can use them independently.

A warp hole shortens a route you can already reach. It never skips a locked gate, required boss, key or rescue step, and the ordinary stairs still provide a way back. It preserves your facing and stops your previous momentum.

If the arrival is occupied or unsafe, you stay where you are. Clear the landing and try again. A refused first traversal leaves the pair dormant. Regeneration replaces both endpoints with a fresh dormant pair.

For an administrator preview, use lod_event_preview_generate warp_hole. This unranked single-event preview can show the pair before Dungeon Level 5. Redeploy after generation and follow the printed locators.

chapters.title: Pay the toll — or find the collateral
text: A bribe blockade closes a required route until one Hero surrenders at least 50 $DEB of equipment value. It opens for the whole party. No cash leaves your wallet; excess item value is not returned as change.

You always have a route to a lost-property cache on the approachable side. Press E at the cache to earmark its generated ring as shared collateral. The ring stays safely in the cache until payment: it cannot be worn, sold, discarded or lost. Finding it never consumes your equipment.

Press E at the toll terminal to review payment. Choose the recovered ring, or select 1–8 of your own unequipped procedural wearables worth at least 50 in total. Weapons, consumables, protected or free starting gear and DFT-created equipment are excluded. Heroes do not pool partial payments.

Read the item names and total, then confirm. Cancel or close the review to spend nothing. Reviews expire after 45 seconds; moving away or changing your inventory, Hero or life invalidates payment. Use the terminal again to retry. Another Hero’s completed payment opens the barrier without charging you.

The passage stays open until this dungeon generation ends. Late arrivals see the same open state. Regeneration replaces the toll and collateral; completed payments are not refunded. The blockade never bypasses the normal keycard, boss or rescue sequence.

Administrator preview: lod_event_preview_generate bribe_blockade. Redeploy and follow the printed terminal and cache locators. The preview is unranked and any confirmed payment uses the actual selected equipment.

chapters.title: Deborah's parting advice
steps: The clock pauses in staging and starts when the first Hero deploys. Every new dungeon gives you thirty minutes.
Keep a useful spell selected. A bottle in your hand means you are holding a bottle—not casting.
Move sideways out of committed charges. A longer corridor is not always a safer escape.
Compare gear drawbacks as carefully as benefits. Keep your permanent feat requirements in mind.
Use short map checks, read the current objective, and remember the stairs.
When the Warden falls, finish the job. At Level 20, defeat Hector too. Then Jail Key, jail door, rescue target.
chapters.quote: You've read the book. Now make yourself useful.

chapters.title: Skeleton of a Hero
rows: Fighter, Rogue or Wizard, chosen when the dungeon is built.
Defeat the Skeleton once; the route opens for everyone.
text: A Skeleton of a Hero guards a required passage. Its name begins “Skeleton of” and comes from the same name generator as your Hero. Its abilities, identity perks, class growth, health dice and eligible automatic feats use the ordinary Hero framework, with AI choices restricted to abilities its controller can use.

The Fighter closes in for melee, the Rogue fires SMG bursts, and the Wizard warns before striking a ground arc. Wizard arcs spend 12 base Magic plus their Content cost, modified by ordinary offensive Magic rules. Wizards cycle their generated Contents and must regenerate when their Magic runs low. Shared defenses, status effects and class rules still apply.

The Skeleton is always on the approachable side of its barrier. Fight it before crossing. A legitimate defeat opens the tall barrier for every Hero, including later arrivals; your normal keycard, boss and rescue sequence remains intact. Regenerating the dungeon creates a fresh encounter.

Combat XP follows ordinary killing-blow and damage-contribution rules, and normal individualized enemy drops apply. There is no extra cash, DFT or guaranteed equipment award. Removing the enemy is not a combat victory.
Administrator preview: lod_event_preview_generate skeleton_blockade. Redeploy and follow the printed location. The preview is unranked.

chapters.title: The Game Master: know what you wear
rows: One attempt per account per dungeon. Decline freely.
One DFT, only when collection succeeds.
The real worn item is stolen.
30 seconds after acceptance; the dungeon keeps running.
text: A suspiciously familiar grin waits in an optional hidden alcove. Press E at the Game Master and read his offer. You have 30 seconds to accept. Your task is to identify one piece of equipment you are wearing among two plausible phonies. The three cards show names, slots and properties. You cannot consult Equipment, Character Sheet, Wallet or the other Player Menu pages while answering.

Only ordinary procedural wearables are at risk. Weapons, consumables, protected or bound gear, free starting items and DFT-created equipment are excluded. Paired gloves count as one item and occupy both hands. No eligible equipment, a full eight-token DFT collection or unavailable reward storage means no accepted attempt.

Answer within 30 seconds. A wrong submitted answer removes the selected real item and its equipment effects. Cancelling, closing, timing out, dying, disconnecting, moving out of range or line of sight, or losing the current challenge forfeits the attempt without theft or reward. The world does not pause or protect you.

A correct answer earns one persistent, server-local DFT with no cash value. If storage fails after your answer, the result reads pending rather than success. Your menus reopen; use the same Game Master to retry the same frozen reward while the same Hero life, worn item and dungeon remain valid. Losing that binding forfeits an uncollected reward.

The Game Master disappears for you after your attempt ends. Other Heroes retain their own independent attempt and may play simultaneously. Reconnecting, changing Heroes or regenerating this dungeon does not grant another attempt. A new dungeon does. Late arrivals see the encounter appropriate to their own account.

Administrator preview: lod_event_preview_generate equipment_quiz. Redeploy with eligible ordinary wearable equipment and follow the printed locator. The preview is unranked but confirmed play risks actual equipment and awards a persistent DFT.
